composing_text: Panzer Regiment 3; Panzergrenadier Regiment 2; Panzergrenadier Regiment 304
current_activity: marching from Amiens toward the battle area
notes: Began move from Amiens to the battle area night of 9-10 June; on 10 June strung out between Amiens and Alencon, not expected in strength until 13 June; arrived without tanks at first.
Counter-attacked 13 June between Cahagnes and Villers-Bocage with two infantry regiments and two artillery battalions but no tanks.

current_activity: 2nd Panzer Division attack toward the Brécey-St. Hilaire road stopped at le Mesnil-Adelée
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 463: the main effort in the center; the right column rolled through le Mesnil-Tôve to le Mesnil-Adelée, where just west of the village it met resistance that forced a halt shortly after daybreak, 7 August, three miles short of the initial objective; the left column advanced through Bellefontaine and almost to Juvigny. Location: le Mesnil-Adelée, the place where the right column was halted. Location caveat: the left column stopped near Juvigny; the point is the right column halt. Opponents: American artillery and antitank pieces north and south of the Sée River kept the wedges immobile (p. 463); elements of the 3d Armored and 30th Infantry Divisions were identified in the zone (ch. 24 p. 461).

current_activity: 2nd Panzer Division armored elements reach St. Lambert about 1000; Luettwitz leads an attack across the Dives bridge
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 548-549: the corps order reached the division about 1900 on 19 August; Luettwitz held off until 0400, 20 August; only the armored elements and part of an armored infantry regiment reached St. Lambert in good order about 1000, and Luettwitz led an attack across the river into the village over the Dives bridge. Location: St. Lambert (Saint-Lambert-sur-Dives). Opponents: Allied artillery fire descended on the columns when the fog lifted (p. 548-549).
